description: Plays a whole arrangement you wrote in one call — film scoring, orchestral arrangement, background music, a song or instrumental (a film cue, a string quartet, a big-band chart): each part played by its doseedo instrument, one stem per part from bar 1 at your tempo, plus a summed mix. Input ONE of: parts[] ({name, instrument, timbre_preset?, lora_id?, players?, notes[]} — doseedo_instruments calls), midi_url (multi-track SMF), or musicxml_url (notation played as marked, at concert pitch). A file's parts are matched by name, then GM program; name any part with instruments {"<part name or index>": {instrument, timbre_preset?, players?}}. A chord on a one-line instrument is split into voices (one stem each). ★ SECTIONS: an instrument is ONE player; give a part players: N (2–8) and its line is played by N different players, summed into ONE section stem — an orchestra = violins I / II, violas, cellos, basses as five parts with players 6 / 6 / 4 / 4 / 3, horns 2–4 in unison; a choir = S/A/T/B parts on "choir" (Carmen, "choir:hp", "choir:m2" or YOUR singer: parts[].timbre_audio_url), which SINGS parts[].lyrics ("Ooh" without), players 4–8 (recipe "choir"); a solo: no players. The WHOLE orchestra in one call: ≤ 32 lines and ≤ 96 player rows (players: N = N rows), any instruments together, ≤ 600 s. Drums: the drum model is a real kit, drum_engine "oneshot" a drum machine. Synth parts: doseedo_render_midi. Timing: bpm and/or tempo_map ([{beat, bpm}]; doseedo_tempo_map lands film hits on downbeats). Result: parts[{name, instrument, url, fit, timbre, lora, players}] — fit.verdict / coverage = did it PLAY its notes (a failed part is re-rolled once; fit.rolls.missed = a roll not played as one), lora.applied = its adapter played — plus mix_url. Next: doseedo_mix {from_job}, then doseedo_session_from_stems {from_job, mix_job}. Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (~1–4 min). Cancel: a render that has not reached the GPU yet is stopped and its credits refunded; one already rendering finishes on the GPU (its credits are spent), the job ends as canceled and the output is discarded.

bpm.description: Tempo of the parts (10–400). Required with parts[] unless tempo_map is given; on a file it sets the speed and keeps the score's fermatas / rit. / tempo changes.

duration_seconds.description: Render length (default: the last note + 2 s; ≤ 600).

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

instruments.description: Name the instrument for any part: {"Violin I": {"instrument": "violin", "players": 6}, "2": {"instrument": "acoustic_guitar", "timbre_preset": "koto:preset1"}, "Choir": {"instrument": "choir", "players": 6, "lyrics": "Glo-ri-a"}} — key = the part name or its 0-based index; players makes a MIDI / MusicXML part a section, lyrics gives a sung part its words (as parts[].lyrics), timbre_audio_url / timbre_audio_urls its own singer or sound (as parts[]: {"Soprano": {"timbre_audio_url": "https://…/singer.wav"}}), drum_engine "oneshot" (+ drum_genre) plays a file's drum part on a one-shot kit ({"Drums": {"drum_engine": "oneshot"}} — no instrument keeps the part's own). Wins over the name/program match.

midi_url.description: Alternative to parts: a multi-track Standard MIDI File (≤ 2 MiB) — a doseedo result link or a public https URL. Channel 10 = drums: the kit, or the one percussion instrument a part is named for (Bass Drum, Cymbals, Bass Drum & Cymbals, Triangle…). A track's CC11 lane (CC1 on a wind / brass / string / bass part) is its written dynamics: a held note swells as it says.

mix.description: Also bounce a summed mix of the stems (default true).

musicxml_url.description: Alternative to parts: a MusicXML score (.musicxml / .xml / .mxl, ≤ 8 MiB) exported from Dorico, Sibelius, Finale, MuseScore, or written by you — or a MuseScore file itself (.mscz / .mscx), read with all its markings.

name.description: Optional: a name for this job's files, e.g. "rainy-loop-3". Every file it returns downloads as <name>_<part>.<ext> (rainy-loop-3_Celesta.wav, rainy-loop-3_rough-mix.wav; one take: rainy-loop-3.wav), so the user can find them. Give each job its own name (a second take: "rainy-loop-3b"). Default: doseedo-<last 6 characters of the job id>.

parts.description: The parts you wrote: [{name?, instrument, timbre_preset?, lora_id?, players?, lyrics?, notes:[{pitch, start_beats, duration_beats, velocity?, lyric?}], dynamics?}] — beats from bar 1, concert pitch. lyrics / lyric: a choir part's words. instrument/timbre_preset = a doseedo_instruments call. players = how many play the line: 1 (default) a soloist, 2–8 a SECTION (e.g. Violins I players 6).

drum_engine.description: A drum / percussion part: "model" (default) = the drum model — a drummer playing the kit in a room (cymbals ring, hits vary, ghost notes speak): the sound for any acoustic kit, rock to jazz to a film cue. A take may drop or add a hit (parts[].fit.voices: missing / extra): render the part again for another take. "oneshot" = a one-shot kit generated for drum_genre, one sample per drum: every written hit lands exactly as written (a half-time bar stays half-time, a stop-time hit stays a hit), but it sounds programmed — the kit for electronic / drum-machine genres only (house, trap, 808). An acoustic kit (drum_kit: rock, punk, jazz, soul, a band seen playing) stays on the model, never oneshot — and a kit whose drum_genre is real drums (funk, boom bap, lo-fi, breakbeat: a sampled break is a drummer; its dust comes from the mix, doseedo_mix style "1990s-hiphop" / "lofi-hiphop") plays on drum_kit whatever is asked (warnings say so). A take that drops a hit is rendered again. Its pads (GM): kick 35/36, snare 38/40, rim 37, clap 39, hats 42/44/46, toms 41–50, crash 49/57, ride 51/59, tambourine 54, cowbell 56, bongos 60/61, congas 62–64, shaker 69/70/82, guiro 73/74, claves 75, woodblock 76/77, triangle 80/81.

drum_genre.description: With drum_engine "oneshot": the kit's genre / words, e.g. "house", "techno", "trap", "synthwave": a dry drum-machine kit. A real-drums genre ("boom bap", "lo-fi", "breakbeat", "funk") puts the part on the drum model's drum_kit. Default: the instrument.

dynamics.description: The part's written LEVEL over time, as a DAW automation lane: [{beat, velocity 1–127}] in beat order, linear between points, a step = two points on one beat, held after the last (p 52, mf 80, f 96, ff 112). A velocity says how a note STARTS; this says how it goes on — a crescendo on a held note: [{beat: 0, velocity: 52}, {beat: 8, velocity: 96}]. Its tone follows it, through a held note too, and doseedo_mix {from_job} rides the level to it. A MusicXML score's dynamics + hairpins arrive as this lane on their own.

dynamics_curve.description: What colours this part's TONE over time: auto (default) = its dynamics lane when that moves, else its note velocities when they vary — soft darker, loud brighter, on every instrument but drums; off = one colour throughout; velocity = the velocities even with a lane; cc11/cc1 = that MIDI CC lane (a midi_url part). Receipt: parts[].dynamics.

lyrics.description: A SUNG part (instrument "choir"): the words it sings, ONE SYLLABLE PER NOTE in time order, a new line per sung phrase — a chord's notes share an onset, so every voice sings that syllable. Hyphens split a word's syllables ("Glo-ri-a in ex-cel-sis De-o"), "_" alone holds the previous syllable over the next note (a melisma), one word ("Ah", "Mm") is sung on every note. Omit = "Ooh" on every note. notes[].lyric places syllables one by one instead (it wins). Other instruments ignore it.

lyric.description: A sung part: the syllable this note sings ("glo-" = more of the word follows, "a", "_" = hold the previous syllable).

players.description: How many players play this line: 1 (default) = a soloist; 2–8 = a SECTION — the line played by that many different players (each its own recording and performance), summed into ONE section stem. A string section = violins I, violins II, violas, cellos, basses with players 4–8 each; a choir section = singers (Soprano players 6 = six sopranos). Each player renders (and costs) like a part.

timbre_audio_url.description: This part's OWN timbre: a recording of the singer (a choir part) or sound it should take on (a drum part too: a kit, a ride or a snare recording on the drum model — not drum_engine "oneshot" or a sampled instrument, which play their own samples) — an https URL, or the audio_key doseedo_get_upload_url returned for a file on your machine. The first 30 s are used; a clean solo take of the voice, 10–30 s, works best. Wins over the preset's voice; a choir part keeps the choir's adapter and sings in THIS voice. receipt: parts[].timbre.

timbre_audio_urls.description: Several recordings (≤ 6): a section's players (players: N) and a split chord's voices take them in turn — a choir section of several singers of your own.

tune.description: false = this part exactly as rendered (no light intonation pass; default true).

vaefix.description: false = this part's decode exactly as rendered (no VAE spectral corrector; default true).

score_key.description: Alternative to parts: a score file on YOUR machine — doseedo_get_upload_url {filename: "cue.mid" | "cue.musicxml" | "cue.mscz"} → PUT the file → its score_key (kept 24 h). A big score sent as a file, not as notes in this call.

score_url.description: Alternative to parts: a score file URL — MIDI, MusicXML or a MuseScore .mscz / .mscx, told apart by its content.

seed.description: Random seed (reuse to re-render close to the same performance).

tempo_map.description: Tempo changes [{beat, bpm}] (first point at beat 0). Overrides a file's own tempo.

tune.description: Light intonation on every winds / brass / strings part (default true): held, clearly pitched notes the model rendered 15–85 cents off are moved toward their written pitch, to a small natural residual — attacks, vibrato and fast notes as played. Receipt: parts[].tune. false = every part as rendered (or parts[].tune false for one).

vaefix.description: VAE spectral corrector on every winds / brass / strings part (default true): the decoder's low-mid fog under each instrument's register is trimmed, mic hiss removed only where present. Receipt: parts[].vaefix. false = every decode as rendered (or parts[].vaefix false for one).

name: doseedo_render_score
title: Render a whole score
